outcome_detail: No resolution reported as of mid-2026; 2026 coverage continues to describe the Baldwin-related suits as active litigation against the provincial government. Baldwin denies all allegations.
criminal_detail: No criminal charges have been laid in relation to the allegations; the plaintiffs' lawyer said the women chose civil suits because they lost confidence in the criminal courts.
description: In the second of two lawsuits filed March 28, 2024 (amended April 29, 2024) in the Supreme Court of Newfoundland and Labrador, a woman alleges that in 2014 an on-duty Royal Newfoundland Constabulary officer, Sgt. Robert Baldwin, drove her home from a night of drinking in downtown St. John's, entered her house under the guise of helping her, and then had non-consensual sex with her, resulting in physical injuries. The statement of claim names the Government of Newfoundland and Labrador, which is responsible for the force, as the sole defendant, and alleges the RNC knew Baldwin was frequently in downtown St. John's outside his assigned area and did nothing to investigate, discipline or control him. Baldwin, who has since retired, denies all allegations through his lawyer. The allegations have not been tested in court.
notes: Companion record rec-80 covers the first suit filed the same day by a different plaintiff (2012 allegations). Other companion records from the same scandal: rec-78 (RNC officer's suit, Jan. 2022) and rec-79 (seven-women suit, Sept. 2022). These 2024 filings brought the total to four civil cases involving ten women.

confidence_notes: The 2014 allegation in this record is distinct from the 2014 allegation in rec-78 (that plaintiff is an RNC officer; this plaintiff is a civilian, and reporting treats them as separate suits). Coverage reports the two March 2024 suits together; incident-to-record assignment follows the order in the CBC/Canadian Press reporting. Plaintiff names are under publication ban. 'Ongoing' is based on May 2026 coverage describing the suits as active; no settlement, dismissal, or trial has been reported.
